mappings.applicability_reason: The tuning job is an automated pipeline that incorporates the vendor's base model as a third-party component before producing the served artifact (evd-002), which is exactly the second applicable_conditions entry -- 'builds incorporate third-party components' -- read broadly enough to cover an ML fine-tuning job rather than only a code build.
assumptions: Treating the weekly fine-tuning run as a 'build' that incorporates a third-party component, consistent with the catalog's instruction that acceptable_implementations are non-exhaustive and the question is whether the mechanism the documentation describes meets the statement -- here, the documentation describes no mechanism at all for identifying or controlling the incoming base model.

mappings.applicability_reason: Tuned artifacts are produced weekly and served to every agent via the reply service (evd-002, evd-004), meeting the applicable condition that tuned artifacts are produced and served; the non_applicable_conditions entry ('no tuned artifact leaves the experiment that produced it') does not hold because artifacts are actively served.

documentation_gaps.title: Base model provenance and transfer integrity are undocumented
documentation_gaps.description: The system overview states that the tuning job fine-tunes the vendor's base reply model (evd-002), but it does not describe how that base model is authenticated or verified before use -- no version pin, checksum, signature, or provenance check is mentioned, and the transfer's authentication and encryption are not addressed anywhere in the document.
documentation_gaps.importance: A base model substituted or tampered with in transit or at the vendor would carry that tampering into the tuned artifact and every suggested reply served to agents; whether any check exists at the point the model enters the tuning job determines whether this dependency is controlled or simply trusted.
requested_evidence: Description of authentication used for the base-model transfer from the vendor
Description of any integrity or provenance verification (checksum, signature, pinned version) applied to the base model before fine-tuning

documentation_gaps.title: Tuned artifacts are named by date only, not by lineage
documentation_gaps.description: The artifact bucket names each week's artifact by export date and serves whichever is most recent (evd-004); the documentation does not state that the base model identity or the training-data snapshot version used to produce each artifact is recorded anywhere.
documentation_gaps.importance: Without recorded lineage, a served artifact traced back to a compromised base model or poisoned training snapshot cannot be identified or scoped after the fact, which matters directly to containing an incident of the kind this threat describes.
requested_evidence: A registry or metadata record naming the base model version and training-data snapshot associated with each artifact

catalog_gap_candidates.concern: No catalog requirement asks that an externally supplied AI base model be verified for integrity or provenance before it is incorporated into a fine-tuning pipeline. The tuning job here receives the vendor's base model across a trust boundary with no documented authentication, encryption, or integrity check (evd-002), and a compromised base model would propagate silently into every tuned artifact and every suggested reply -- a supply-chain risk distinct from training-corpus governance or generic dependency management.

nearest_requirements.why_not: Addresses how a deployment pipeline authenticates to its environments and how third-party software components enter a build (e.g., pinned dependency manifests); it is written for code/dependency supply chains and does not name integrity verification of an externally supplied model's weights as its own artifact class.

Asks that a served tuned artifact's lineage -- its base model and training-data version -- be recorded after the fact, which helps trace an incident but does not ask that the incoming base model be verified for integrity or provenance before training begins.

Covers adoption and per-request authentication of external tool servers reached over a defined protocol (e.g., MCP); a base model transferred once for fine-tuning is not a tool server and no such protocol is in use here.
